questions.solution_text:
$3e^2$ is a constant coefficient multiplying $x$.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x + 3e^2(1)$
$= e^x + 3e^2$

questions.question_text: What is the equation of the tangent to $y=2e^x$ at $x=0$?

options.why: omitted the $y$-intercept $+2$ from the tangent equation

questions.question_text: At which point on the curve $y=e^x$ is the tangent line parallel to the line $y=ex+4$?

options.why: used gradient $1$ instead of matching the parallel line gradient $e$
substituted $x=e$ instead of solving the gradient equation $e^x = e$
used an incorrect $y$-coordinate that does not lie on $y=e^x$

questions.solution_text:
Parallel lines have equal gradients, so tangent gradient $m=e$.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^x = e^1 \implies x = 1$.
When $x=1$, $y = e^1 = e$.
Point is $(1, e)$.
